question: Zomato SDE-1 interview (on campus, GeeksforGeeks experience). One of the questions asked the candidate to **implement backend request-handling logic in Go using goroutines and channels**, including **timeouts** and **edge cases**. The exact request-handling task was not recorded, so the usual version is a worker pool that processes a set of requests concurrently with per-request timeouts.
lookingFor: Avoiding goroutine leaks, deadlocks and data races
Edge-case awareness: empty input, closed channels, errors, shutdown
followUps: How would you detect and avoid goroutine leaks?
What is the difference between a buffered and an unbuffered channel here?
How do you propagate cancellation through an HTTP server handler?
How would you add rate limiting or back-pressure to this pool?
